main_text.l: num jucunditatem allecti relinquant, ne venationibus dediti, latro-cinijs assuefcant, & ne species animalium devastentur per nimiam venationem ac similes ob causas interdicere posse. 3. Principes alios q superioritatis jura habentes ob publicum interesse inter eos ipsos subditos q venationi jura obtinet, certu venandi modu prscribere posse, quotiescúq, publica utilitas id exigat. Diss. Joh. Faber & alij in §. feræl nst. de rer. div. horum Contradicentium argum. dissolvunt Fach. Zoan. d.d.lo. & Eber. Speckhan qq. J. cent. 1. qu. 97. Sic ergo agricolis in venationibus certum modum præscripsit Fridericus Imper. in c. 1. §. si quis rusticus vers. nemo retia de pace tenenda in usf. Feud. Sic Jus civile in itineribus frequentatis foveas facere & tendiculas ponere ad capiendas feras nulla monitione præcedente prohibet l. qui fovéas 28. ff. ad L. Aquil. Sic idem Jus Civile piscatoribus noctu in litore maris ignem accendere interdicit, ne decipiantur nauta putantes ad portum se appelere l. ne piscatores ff. de incend. ruin. & naufr. Sic Jus Saxon interdicit omnem venationem Si segesjam[?] in articulos sic ge-nicula surrexit Sandrecht[?] lib. 2. art. 61. Sic Jus Saxon feram in alie-

nam sylvam tendentem cum canibus non nisi absq; in flatu cornu-culi venatorij persequi concedit Landrecht[?] lib.2.art. 61. Sic idem Jus Saxonum alienum fundum venandi gratia ingredi non modò tùm quando dominus id prohibet Weichbild sub tit. das man auff an-dern Bürfern nicht jagen soll/& gloss. Weichbilds art.122. sed & generaliter ipso jure licet per præscriptionem in alieno fundo venandi Jus acquisierint, sub pœna centum florenorum in ordinat.Provinc von jagen/hegen und Hünerfangen interdicit. page.notes: The scan shows only the lower part of the page. Doubtful readings: "Landrecht" (printed in a form that may be Sanorecht), "Saxonici" (printed as "Saxgnici"), and "Illustrissim" at the right edge, which may continue past the cut. Black-letter passages are marked with bl; the boundary between black letter and roman is uncertain in places. "statis" is printed "slatis". A small isolated mark "1" stands at the centre foot; I did not treat it as a page number. The left-edge fragments (o, k, de, s., tis, in, di, fu, locus, actu, quod, opis, atio, um) are cut-off margin text and are not transcribed. No running head or page number is visible.
